predecessors.note: "Established: 1728, under the Maratha Peshwas" (infobox: Part of the Maratha Empire 1728-1804); Baji Rao I received a share of Chhatrasal's domains ("the bequest of one-third of the Maharaja's dominions upon his death", undated), and "In 1742, Naro Shanker was made the Subahdar of Jhansi".

successors.note: Annexed in 1853 under the doctrine of lapse and taken after the fall of the fort on 5 April 1858; "In 1861, the city and a dependent territory were ceded to Gwalior State" and "returned to British rule in exchange for the Gwalior Fort and the cantonment of Morar" in 1886.

capitals.name: Jhansi
capitals.note: Infobox Capital: Jhansi, a fortified town; Bir Singh Deo of Orchha built the fort in 1613-1618 (the page).

rulers.name: Naro Shanker
rulers.note: Subahdar from 1742 for about 15 years, recalled in 1757.

rulers.name: Shiv Rao Hari Bhau
rulers.note: Took the title Rao in 1804; "In 1804 British protection was promised to the Maratha subedar".

rulers.name: Gangadhar Rao
rulers.note: "the British rulers accepted Gangadhar Rao his brother as the Raja of Jhansi in 1843"; died November 1853.

rulers.name: Rani Lakshmibai
rulers.note: From August 1857 to June 1858 in the page text; the defenders left the fort on 5 April 1858 (Siege page).

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, no Cliopatria row. The page gives 4,059 km2 for 1804 and no boundary or other year; a 36 km circle about Jhansi (about 4,050 km2, ratio 1.0) stands in for all years. Inside the Maratha Empire shape until the British treaty of 1804.

ledger.note: 1728: Jhansi is established under the Maratha Peshwas. Infobox "Established: 1728"; the text has the Subahdar Naro Shanker appointed only in 1742. The extent is the 1804 area as a circle (my reading); the page gives no earlier extent.

1853: the East India Company annexes Jhansi under the doctrine of lapse but does not take it. "the British East India Company, under Governor-General Lord Dalhousie, applied the Doctrine of Lapse" and rejected the adopted heir Damodar Rao (Gangadhar Rao died in November 1853); the Doctrine of lapse page lists "Jhansi (1853)". The page says the state was "annexed in 1853 and not brought under British control until November 1858", so 1853 to 1858 is carried as a contest. The mutiny of 8 June 1857 and the Rani's rule of "August 1857 to January 1858" are on the same page.

5 April 1858: the fort of Jhansi falls. Hugh Rose "laid siege to Jhansi on 24 March" and "on 5 April the defenders abandoned the fort". The Jhansi State page says British control came only in November 1858 and the Rani died of wounds at Kotah ki Serai near Gwalior on 17 or 18 June 1858.

5 April 1858: Jhansi State ends with the fall of the fort. "between 24 March and 5 April 1858"; infobox of the state page "Indian rebellion: 1858". The Jhansi State page has the November 1858 date for control of the state.

wars.name: Siege of Jhansi
wars.outcome: Rani Lakshmibai ruled Jhansi from August 1857; Hugh Rose besieged it from 24 March to 5 April 1858 and the defenders abandoned the fort on 5 April.
wars.note: Jhansi State page: the mutiny "massacred the European officers of the garrison along with their wives and children on 8 June 1857"; "From August 1857 to January 1858 Jhansi under the Rani's rule was at peace".

certainty.note: The page gives the 1804 area and no boundary; the shape is a circle of that area for all years.

sources.title: Jhansi State
sources.note: Established 1728 under the Maratha Peshwas; Naro Shanker subahdar from 1742; British protection promised in 1804; treaty of 18 November 1817; Gangadhar Rao accepted 1843; doctrine of lapse 1853; 1857 mutiny and the Rani; ceded to Gwalior 1861, exchanged 1886; area 4,059 km2 (1804).

sources.title: Siege of Jhansi
sources.note: Hugh Rose laid siege on 24 March 1858; the defenders abandoned the fort on 5 April 1858; silent on Gwalior and 1861.

sources.title: Doctrine of lapse
sources.note: Lists Jhansi (1853) among the states the Company took over, with Satara (1848), Nagpur (1854 in the text, 1853 in the table), Jaitpur and Sambalpur (1849) and Udaipur in Chhattisgarh (1852).

notes: Three pages opened (Jhansi State, Siege of Jhansi, Doctrine of lapse). Conflicts: annexation 1853 (text, Doctrine of lapse) against control only in November 1858 (state page) against the fall of the fort on 5 April 1858 (Siege page); infobox end 1858; the exchange with Gwalior in 1886 (Jhansi State page) against 1885 in the gwalior-state dossier (Gwalior State page) - the Siege page is silent on the 1861 cession to Gwalior. The british-empire dossier should record the vassal_start from the British protection promised in 1804 (treaty of 18 November 1817 for hereditary rulers) to 1853. The cession of Jhansi city to Gwalior (1861) and its return (1886 here, 1885 there) belong to the gwalior-state dossier. Orchha (Bir Singh Deo, builder of the fort 1613-1618) needs a dossier from this region if it is to be mapped.
